candidates.title: The Hive That Hummed at Midnight
story_beats: At the snowy meadow, rabbit and fox discovered the empty exhibition beehive hummed every night after the museum closed before the library opened, leaving the visiting readers waiting.
Rabbit attempted an immediate fix, but the curator sealed the display case but the humming grew louder; fox stopped the attempt before the situation worsened.
Fox examined the evidence and realized a ventilation fan below the exhibit vibrated a loose wooden panel at one particular speed; together they revised their plan rather than repeating the mistake.
With the visiting readers watching, they secured the panel and tested the ventilation before reopening the exhibit, then explained the clue so their neighbors could prevent the problem next time.

candidates.title: The Ferry That Drifted Sideways
story_beats: At the snowy meadow, rabbit and fox discovered the small demonstration ferry slid sideways despite its guide rope being taut before the library opened, leaving the visiting readers waiting.
Rabbit attempted an immediate fix, but the crew pulled the rope tighter but the ferry moved further off course; fox stopped the attempt before the situation worsened.
Fox examined the evidence and realized the guide pulley had rotated out of alignment and was pulling at an angle; together they revised their plan rather than repeating the mistake.

With the visiting readers watching, they stopped the demonstration and realigned the pulley under a supervised safety check, then explained the clue so their neighbors could prevent the problem next time.

candidates.title: The Lanterns That Would Not Rise
story_beats: At the snowy meadow, rabbit and fox discovered the festival's paper lantern models stayed on the ground despite warm air inside before the library opened, leaving the visiting readers waiting.
Rabbit attempted an immediate fix, but the builders added heavier lamps but the models sank even faster; fox stopped the attempt before the situation worsened.
Fox examined the evidence and realized a recent coating had made the paper too heavy for the small warm-air lift; together they revised their plan rather than repeating the mistake.

With the visiting readers watching, they replaced the coating with lighter safe display material and tested stationary models, then explained the clue so their neighbors could prevent the problem next time.
